extracted.intended_audience: Authors of MathML markup and MathML renderer implementers (web developers, accessibility tool authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and normative rules for authoring and implementing MathML presentation markup, including element/attribute semantics, defaulting rules, whitespace, directionality, linebreaking, and rendering behaviors. Intended for people writing MathML or implementing renderers or accessibility transforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default value sources (inherited, automatic, operator dictionary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Default values described as inherited or automatic; a third source is a MathML operator dictionary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inherited defaults are taken from the rendering environment (mstyle or surrounding element attributes) and never depend on the content or attributes of the same element. Automatic defaults should be computed by a renderer to produce high-quality rendering and may depend on element content and context. A MathML operator dictionary may provide global default behavior (see B. Operator Dictionary and 3.2.5.6.1). The value used will always be one that could have been specified explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributes shared by all MathML elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain attributes are allowed on every MathML element (plus xml: namespace attributes and external namespaces which are ignored by default).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attributes include id (unique identifier for linking/parallel markup), xref (idref to another element), class (style classes for CSS), style (inline CSS), href (URI for hyperlinks; not supported on all elements), and the intent and arg attributes for annotating intent. See 2.1.6 for details and 7.5 for CSS interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: intent and arg attributes for semantic annotations
rubrics_metrics.description: All MathML presentation elements accept intent and arg attributes to support specifying intent (for audio/braille guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: intent is an intent expression giving intended meaning; arg names an element to be referenced from an intent expression on an ancestor element. More fully described in section 5 (Annotating MathML: intent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitespace collapsing in token elements
rubrics_metrics.description: MathML ignores whitespace outside token elements; whitespace inside token elements (except <cs>) is normalized by trimming and collapsing sequences to a single U+0020.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leading and trailing whitespace is removed; internal sequences of whitespace are replaced by a single space. To encode leading/trailing or multiple spaces, use non-breaking space U+00A0 or other non-trimmed characters. xml:space is not relevant for this trimming; XML processors pass whitespace in tokens to MathML processor. For whitespace outside token contents, use <mspace/> rather than an <mtext> containing only whitespace entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-level <math> element requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Every MathML expression must be wrapped in an outermost <math> element; a <math> element must not contain another <math>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The math element encapsulates each instance of MathML markup, is the root for MathML content, can contain arbitrary child elements and they render by default as if in an mrow. Applies to cut-and-paste and interapplication transfer (see 7.3 Transferring MathML).

rubrics_metrics.name: <math> element accepts common presentation and shared attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: The math element accepts mathematics presentation attributes and attributes shared by all MathML elements (e.g., dir, mathbackground).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: dir sets overall directionality (defaults to ltr on the math element but inherits on others). mathbackground sets background color of bounding box similar to mstyle. See 3.1.5 for directionality and 3.1.9 for presentation attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: display attribute semantics on <math> (block vs inline)
rubrics_metrics.description: display can be 'block' or 'inline' and controls whether the expression renders as a separate vertical block or inline with text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When display=block, displaystyle is initialized to true; when display=inline, displaystyle false; scriptlevel initialized to 0 in both cases. Block math should be treated as block-level for spacing/linebreaking; inline should be treated as inline (no spaces/line breaks inserted before punctuation). When missing, renderer may initialize appropriate to context.

rubrics_metrics.name: maxwidth attribute on <math>
rubrics_metrics.description: maxwidth is a length specifying the maximum width used for linebreaking; default is the available width in the surrounding environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If available width cannot be determined, renderer should assume infinite rendering width. Inside mtable, column widths act as the line-wrapping width for each cell.

rubrics_metrics.name: overflow attribute on <math> (handling overwide expressions)
rubrics_metrics.description: overflow chooses handling when expression is too long: 'linebreak', 'scroll', 'elide', 'truncate', or 'scale'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: linebreak — break across lines (see 3.1.7); scroll — viewport with scrollbars; elide — abbreviate (e.g., first and last terms with + ... +); truncate — simply cut off (recommended to indicate truncation); scale — choose fonts so expression fits (only if too large). Value comparisons are ASCII case-insensitive. Used when size negotiation not possible or fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: altimg and altimg sizing on <math>
rubrics_metrics.description: altimg is a URI fallback image for user agents that don't support MathML; altimg-width and altimg-height specify how to scale it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only one of altimg-width/height is given, preserve aspect ratio. If neither given, use natural image size. altimg-valign controls vertical alignment (length or keywords 'top'|'middle'|'bottom'), default 0ex and only relevant when display=inline. alttext provides textual alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: cdgroup attribute for OpenMath content dictionaries
rubrics_metrics.description: cdgroup specifies a CD group file that catalogs CD bases for locating OpenMath content dictionaries for csymbol/annotation elements in this math element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When not specified, embedding document format may provide a method; otherwise system must determine a CD base; absent info, http://www.openmath.org/cd is assumed as the CD base for standard CDs maintained by the OpenMath Society. See 4.2.3 Content Symbols <csymbol>.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of special Unicode characters/entities for semantic tokens
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain Unicode characters represent identifiers/operators that render like other symbols or invisibly but are semantically distinct (e.g., U+2146.. for differential d, exponential e, imaginary i; U+2061.. representing function application, invisible times, invisible comma, invisible plus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should use these characters or entities wherever applicable because they influence spacing, linebreaking, and spoken renderings; mglyph inside token elements is neutral for ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Token elements represent individual symbols; layout schemata build structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Token elements (mi,mn,mo,mtext,mspace,ms,mglyph) represent single symbols/numbers/operators; layout schemata (mrow, mfrac, msqrt, etc.) build larger expressions and impose argument roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All individual symbols in a mathematical expression should be represented by token elements (e.g., <mn>24</mn>). Layout schemata attach special meaning to number/position of children; a child is an argument. This structure aids rendering and automatic interpretation. See 3.1.2 and 3.1.8 for element summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required argument counts and inferred <mrow> behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Many elements require a specific number of arguments (1,2,3); some elements listed as requiring 1* accept any number and conceptually treat children as a single inferred mrow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements with 1* (msqrt, mstyle, merror, mpadded, mphantom, menclose, mtd, mscarry, math) accept any number of children and when children are 0 or >1 they form an inferred mrow from all children. Table 3.1.3.2 lists required counts and argument roles (e.g., mfrac has numerator and denominator).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special behaviors of certain presentation elements (space-like, embellishing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some presentation elements have special behaviors such as being space-like or embellishing an operator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Space-like elements defined in 3.2.7 affect rendering rules for mo elements. Elements like msup can embellish operators that are their first argument; 3.2.5 defines embellished operator and how that affects stretchy/operator rendering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall directionality vs token text directionality
rubrics_metrics.description: MathML recognizes two directionalities: overall layout direction (Layout Schemata) and text/symbol direction inside token elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall directionality specified by dir on containing math element (default ltr). When dir=rtl, layout is mirror image of European layout (e.g., subscripts appear to left). dir may be set on math, mrow or mstyle; elements inherit directionality. Terms leading/trailing depend on directionality. Token element text direction is determined by Unicode properties; when mixed direction, apply Unicode Bidi algorithm to each token element independently. Glyph mirroring and shaping should be respected; use appropriate codepoints (e.g., Hebrew cardinals U+2135-U+2138) as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displaystyle and scriptlevel semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation nodes are associated with displaystyle and scriptlevel indicating expansive vertical layout and scripting level; initialized by math element and adjusted by script/limit schemata and certain elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: display attribute on math initializes displaystyle and scriptlevel defaults. Elements like mfrac and mroot typically set displaystyle false and increment scriptlevel for some arguments. displaystyle affects vertical spacing and interpretation of largeop/movablelimits. scriptlevel controls font size; changes multiply current font size by scriptsizemultiplier^(change in scriptlevel) but must not reduce below scriptminsize. scriptsizemultiplier defaults ~sqrt(1/2); scriptminsize defaults to 8pt; these may be changed on any presentation element. mathsize overrides scriptlevel effects on token children; scriptlevel changes are applied before explicit mathsize. scriptlevel can be signed +/- to increment/decrement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where linebreaks may occur (mrow and mfenced) and typical break points
rubrics_metrics.description: Linebreaks (automatic and manual) take place within mrow (including inferred mrow) or mfenced; breaks typically occur at mo elements and for backward compatibility at mspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renderers may place breaks at other points (between mi or within long mn). If a renderer breaks inside such points it should indent following line according to indentation attributes. Automatic linebreaking occurs when math overflow=linebreak and engine determines insufficient width (available width must be known). Forced linebreaks use linebreak=newline on mo or mspace. Both automatic and manual breaks can occur in same formula. Automatic linebreaking of subexpressions of mfrac, msqrt, mroot, menclose and script elements is not required; renderers may ignore forced breaks in those elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributes controlling linebreaking and indentation on mo/mspace
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes on mo and possibly mspace control desirability of a break ('where'), operator display/position when breaking, and indentation of following lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where — determines desirability/inhibition/requirement of break at a specific operator/space (set on mo/mspace). Operator Display/Position — decides whether operator appears at end of line, start of next line, or both, and how much vertical space to add after break; can be set on mo or inherited from mstyle/math. Indentation — determines indentation of line following a break, including aligning to points in previous line; set on mo or inherited from mstyle/math. See 3.2.5.2.2 and 3.2.5.2.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic linebreaking behavior and available width determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic linebreaking requires knowledge of available width; if none can be determined, an infinite width should be assumed; inside mtable, column width used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When overflow=linebreak, renderer must know available width to decide breaks; available width is inherited from environment like font properties. Inside mtable each column's specified or content-determined width should be used as wrapping width and each entry linewrapped as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary roles of presentation elements (token, layout schemata, tables, scripts, enlivening)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise mapping of element names to their roles such as token elements (mi,mn,mo...), general layout schemata (mrow,mfrac,msqrt...), script and limit schemata (msub,msup,...), tables/matrices (mtable,mtr,mtd,...), elementary math layout (mstack,mlongdiv...), and enlivening (maction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate element class depending on role: tokens for symbols, layout schemata to build expressions and enforce argument counts/positions, tables for matrices, script schemata for sub/superscripts, maction to bind actions to subexpressions. See 3.1.8 for the full categorized list and intended semantics.
